title: A gift you would like to buy for your friend
titleVi: Món quà bạn muốn mua cho bạn thân
prompt: Describe a gift you would like to buy for your friend
bullets: how long you have known him/her
how you would choose a gift for him/her
and explain why you would choose that gift for him/her

notes.label: How we met
notes.text: first day of grade 6, seated together

part2.question: Describe a gift you would like to buy for your friend

segments.v: I want to talk about a gift for my best friend Linh. I knew her in grade 6. We sat next to each other in class. I have known her for five years. Her birthday is next month and I want to buy her a film camera. She likes taking photos very much and she always borrows my camera. I will choose the gift carefully. I will read reviews on the internet and go to a camera shop in the Old Quarter. Film cameras are quite expensive so I am saving money now. I choose this gift because she likes photography and it is useful. We can take photos together. I think she will be very happy when she receives it. I hope she will like it.

fluency.band6: Answers the bullets in order with short sentences; ends with two similar hopes (“I think she will… I hope she will…”).
fluency.band9: Introduces the friend with a funny detail (seated by the alphabet), explains how the idea came about, shows real research, and gives a thoughtful reason, ending with a light closing line.

lexical.band6: knew her, likes taking photos, useful, happy.
lexical.band9: inseparable, made up my mind, trendy, doing my homework, putting aside, lights up, treasure, keep it a secret.

grammar.band6: Errors: “I knew her in grade 6” (met), “I choose this gift” (I'd choose). Mostly “will” and simple present.
grammar.band9: Present perfect continuous (I've been doing my homework; I've been putting aside…), passive continuous (broken ones being sold online), “As for…”, and “unlike…”.

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 “I knew her in grade 6” should be “I met her in grade 6” (know is a state, not an event), and “I choose this gift” should be “I'd choose”. Band 9 tells how the idea came about, shows real research, and gives a thoughtful reason for the choice.
